newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, April loses ground.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, April loses ground.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended mixed Monday in a moderate session, with a strong, early short covering rally partly offset later by some technical selling when upside momentum stalled at resistance.
April eased one cent to close at $1.937 per million British thermal units after stalling early at $2.04. May settled 0.2 cent higher at $2.025. Others ended mixed.

"They hit an air pocket (on the upside), then hit some (sell) stops on the way down and scared some of the length out," said one Houston trader, noting prospects for colder East Coast weather this week helped support the cash.

But many said the brief bout of cold this week for northern tier states likely would not be enough to ignite and sustain a significant rally, particularly with storage in good shape and winter drawing to a close.
Technical traders still pegged important resistance in April at $2.04, with further selling likely in the mid-teens and at $2.28. Support was seen at $1.78-1.80 and then at the $1.701 contract low.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed almost five cents Monday to the low-$1.90s. Midcon pipes were talked up slightly in the high-$1.70s. New York city gate swing gas gained more than five cents to the low-$2.20s on colder weather there.
The 12-month strip gained 0.9 cent to $2.126. NYMEX said an estimated 39,369 contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 45,982.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Monday.

On the KCBT, April finished two cents lower at $1.70, while deferreds ended steady to up one-half cent. The East/West spread widened by one cent to 23.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 545 lots changed hands, up from Friday's total of 248.
